title: Credential added to a Microsoft Entra service principal
description: Detects a successful Microsoft Entra audit event that adds authentication credentials to a service principal.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may add a credential to a service principal to establish persistent cloud access.
hypothesis.rationale: A new certificate or secret can let its holder authenticate as the service principal and inherit the application's effective access, although legitimate provisioning and rotation create the same audit activity.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify successful service-principal credential additions while leaving failures, credential removals, general updates, and incomplete events unmatched.

triage.summary: Validate the initiator, target service principal, credential type and lifetime, and the corresponding change record before deciding whether persistence was established.
steps: Identify the initiating user or workload and the target service principal from InitiatedBy and TargetResources.
Confirm the credential type, creation time, expiration, owner, effective permissions, and whether the change is covered by approved provisioning or rotation.
Review adjacent application and service-principal changes, then remove unauthorized credentials and investigate the initiating identity when the change is unexplained.
false_positives: Approved application onboarding, certificate renewal, secret rotation, or automated identity-lifecycle activity

validation.expected_outcome: Match only a successful Add service principal credentials operation; do not match failures, removals, general updates, or events without a result.
